title: Pressing the Ctrl and Alt keys simultaneously causes subsequent actions to behave as if the Ctrl key is being held down.
author: kjin
summary: The repro is specific enough to point at Keyboard Manager’s modifier-state normalization for swapped Ctrl/Win remaps, but the exact stuck-key branch still needs maintainer-side reproduction rather than a blind patch.

judgment.rationale: The issue provides a concrete remap pair, a specific Ctrl+Alt chord, and a manual recovery key, which is enough to investigate the modifier-state machine directly.
evidence: The report swaps Left Ctrl -> Left Win and Left Win -> Left Ctrl, then triggers the bug with Left Ctrl + Alt + 4 in Chrome.
After the chord is released, later scroll operations behave as if Ctrl is still held until Left Ctrl is pressed again.
KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp has explicit modifier reset logic for some remap classes, but it is narrowly targeted at Caps Lock and modifier-to-nonmodifier/text cases.
Current Keyboard Manager tests exercise many modifier remaps, but there is no targeted regression for this exact swapped Ctrl/Win plus Alt chord sequence.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the exact swapped-modifier repro against the Keyboard Manager engine and design a state-normalization fix for modifier-to-modifier remaps that can strand Ctrl/Win state after Alt-generated system-key paths.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked fix exists, and the source still lacks an explicit regression or reset path for the exact modifier-to-modifier chord reported here.

proposed_fixes.title: Resynchronize modifier state for swapped Ctrl/Win remaps across Alt-driven system-key chords
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The most likely bug is a mismatched modifier-down/modifier-up sequence when Ctrl is remapped to Win, Win is remapped back to Ctrl, and Alt causes WM_SYSKEY* delivery. That can leave the engine or the foreground app believing Ctrl is still active until another physical Ctrl transition arrives.
plan: Reproduce the exact Ctrl<->Win swap plus Alt+4 sequence against the engine test harness and a real app surface.
Trace which modifier state remains asserted after source key-up and normalize both injected and suppressed key-up paths for modifier-to-modifier remaps.
Add a focused regression covering the reported sequence and a nearby variant without Chrome-specific behavior.
verification: With Left Ctrl <-> Left Win swaps active, press Ctrl+Alt+4 and confirm subsequent scrolling no longer zooms as if Ctrl remained down.
Verify ordinary Ctrl/Win swaps and unrelated Alt shortcuts still behave correctly.

confidence.rationale: The symptom and current reset coverage point strongly at a modifier-state bug, but the exact stuck-key branch still needs live reproduction or a dedicated failing engine test.

issue_context.summary: A swapped Ctrl/Win mapping leaves the system behaving as though Ctrl is latched after a Ctrl+Alt+4 chord until Ctrl is pressed again.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.100.2 via WinGet.
The remap pair and triggering chord are fully spelled out.
No assignee, linked PR, or follow-up discussion is present.
The reporter identified a reliable manual recovery action: press Left Ctrl once.
inferences: The bug likely sits in Keyboard Manager’s modifier state tracking rather than Chrome itself, because the stuck state persists into later unrelated input handling.
Alt involvement matters because it changes Windows message semantics to WM_SYSKEY*, which is where remap state bugs often diverge.
issue_context.analysis: This is actionable without more reporter input. The remaining uncertainty is in the internal state path, so the correct next step is a maintainer reproduce action rather than a generic log request.
initial_investigation: KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp resets lower-level modifier state only for certain remap classes, leaving a likely gap for modifier-to-modifier swaps that also involve Alt.
SingleKeyRemappingTests.cpp already contains other stuck-key hardening tests, which makes this issue a good candidate for a new targeted engine regression.

actions.label: Approve swapped-modifier state fix design
actions.note: The current hypothesis points to the modifier state machine, but the failing branch still needs a direct repro or failing test.

actions.label: Reproduce stuck Ctrl after Ctrl/Win swap
actions.note: Drive the exact remap pair and Alt-modified chord before choosing a narrower engine patch.

prerequisites: Enable Keyboard Manager and configure Left Ctrl -> Left Win plus Left Win -> Left Ctrl.
Use a desktop app where Ctrl+scroll visibly changes behavior, such as Chrome zoom.
steps: Open the target app and verify the Ctrl/Win swap is active.
Press and release Left Ctrl + Alt + 4 exactly as reported.
Scroll the mouse wheel or perform another Ctrl-sensitive action without pressing Ctrl again.
Press Left Ctrl once and compare behavior before and after that recovery key press.
reproduce.expected_result: After the chord is released, later actions should behave normally without requiring an extra Ctrl press to clear a latched state.
